_comment: A month tab's shape, read out of the workbook itself (exported as .xlsx) rather
than a text rendering of it, on 2026-09-01 MDT. The geometry here is the real
one: an earlier capture taken from the text export was off by one row, which
The tests build their fake sheet from these numbers, so the script is exercised
against the real geometry rather than one invented to suit it. If the sheet's
shape ever changes, recapture this file and the tests follow.

1.D: = Bought for the other person expense not shared

entryRows.A_to_F: empty, but pre-formatted: B and C carry "$"#,##0.00, D carries M/d/yyyy
entryRows.N_to_T: one formula per row, =IF(N$4=$E5,$B5+$C5,0), fanning the amount into its category column

_comment: The convention the legend in D1 names: something one of them bought for the
other, at their request, which is not a shared expense. The amount is entered
as a formula doubling it, so the 50/50 split in row 3 nets out to the other
person owing the whole of it, and the cell is highlighted.
Read from the real entry: B5 on Sept2026 held =34.95*2 on a solid FFFF00 fill,

knownQuirks: The month total in A2 sums B5:B163 but C5:C164 — one row shorter on his side.
A receipt on row 164 paid by Rob would not reach the monthly total. The script
stops where the category formulas stop (row 164), so this only matters if a
month ever runs to 160 receipts; August 2026 used five.
Rows 9 and below carry category formulas that reference 'Oct2025 - Var
Expenses'!N$4 rather than their own header row — an artefact of the tab having
been copied. They agree only because both tabs' headers say the same thing.
